transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Sana Malik (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Raman (Polaris Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Polaris Platform), Ana Gutierrez (Polaris Product), Javier Morales (Polaris Legal)

Summary:
High-level POC scoping to pick an open-model shortlist for a 1-week benchmarking pilot. Focus: biomedical domain document QA, multilingual support (EN/ES/PT), latency SLO ~300-500ms per response for short answers, throughput ~8-10 concurrent requests sustained with bursts to 30, and data isolation requirements (VPC, KMS). Discussed model quality tradeoffs, quantization, dedicated vs hosted, and timeline for delivering benchmarks and pricing.

Topics:
- Success criteria and evaluation metrics (EM/F1 for QA, latency p50/p95, token cost)
- Workload sizing (QPS, concurrency, avg tokens/request)
- Candidate open models and tradeoffs (quality vs latency/cost)
- Security / deployment constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2)
- Timeline and next steps for POC

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros from our side, I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood, and Sana is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Sana: Hi all. Glad to be here. We'll focus on sizing, success metrics, and a short shortlist of open models that make sense for Polaris' biomedical use-case.
[00:16] Priya: Thanks. We're trying to evaluate open models for document QA across clinical notes and research articles, need Spanish and Portuguese support too, and we have sensitive patient-adjacent data so we need either Private or Dedicated with KMS.
[00:30] Ethan: Understood. Two quick calibration questions: what's your expected concurrency and typical request size?
[00:36] Marcus: We're currently prototyping, but expected live traffic for the POC is about 8-10 concurrent users with occasional bursts to ~30 for demo days. Average prompt + context ~ 800 tokens, responses usually 60-200 tokens depending on the ask.
[00:50] Ana: Success criteria from product: for extractive QA we'd like EM > 75% and F1 > 82% on our annotation set; latency p95 ideally under 800ms for typical doc slices, but for the MVP we can accept p95 < 1.2s. Cost is a big factor too, we want to understand per-1000-token cost.
[01:10] Sana: Helpful. For Redwood POCs we usually run both quality and perf benchmarks: a quality sweep on your labeled set + a perf run that simulates the concurrency and average token sizes you mentioned. We'll also show how batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization impact latency/cost.
[01:28] Priya: On model preferences, we want an open-model shortlist. We're leaning away from closed APIs because of data residency and auditability. Which open models do you recommend for biomedical plus multilingual?
[01:40] Sana: Shortlist candidates we usually consider: Llama-3 family (35B/70B), Mistral Mixtral 8x/Mixtral 7B variants, Llama-2 13B (quantized), Falcon 40B-instruct, and smaller instruction-tuned models like Mistral-Instruct 7B. For biomedical specificity you can also consider adapter fine-tunes or using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to keep base model general but span domain knowledge.
[02:00] Ethan: To add, the tradeoffs are roughly: bigger models (70B) tend to give better out-of-the-box accuracy for complex QA but at higher latency and cost; mid-sized models (13B-20B) with quantization often hit a sweet spot for latency while being surprisingly competent on many tasks, especially with targeted prompt engineering and RAG.
[02:20] Priya: Do you have any benchmarks on biomedical reads? We're worried about hallucinations on clinical facts.
[02:27] Sana: We don't ship a public 'biomedical benchmark' but we run customer-specific evals. For hallucination mitigation we recommend retrieval first (document selection with dense retrievers), strict prompt templates, and evaluation with counters like calibration tests. Also consider running targeted fine-tune or LoRA on a small in-domain dataset if the quality gap remains.
[02:48] Marcus: From infra side, can Redwood run the perf bench in our VPC? We need to test network egress and KMS latency.
[02:55] Ethan: Yes: for Dedicated or Private deployments we can run the benchmarks within your VPC or within Redwood Dedicated capacity in a nearby region	6ms. For a quick start we can also run an initial bench in our hosted environment with anonymized subset, then repeat in your VPC to get realistic numbers.
[03:12] Javier: Legally we need SOC2 reports and data flow diagrams before spinning up anything that touches PHI. Can you share standard security docs?
[03:18] Ethan: Absolutely	6ms I'll attach SOC2, our private deployment security pack, and a sample network diagram. We'll also include the redacted audit log samples.
[03:26] Ana: Back to models	6ms can you recommend which 2-3 models to run in the 1-week pilot given our constraints (latency target, cost sensitivity, multilingual)?
[03:36] Sana: I'd recommend: 1) Mixtral (Mistral Mixtral 8x) as a strong cost-performance baseline for multi-lingual general reasoning; 2) Llama-3 35B (or 70B if quality gap is large) as a high-quality baseline	6ms good for complicated reasoning and long context; 3) Llama-2 13B quantized as a low-latency, low-cost control. If you want a specialized approach, run one RAG setup with a smaller base model + domain retriever.
[03:56] Priya: Why Mixtral specifically for multilingual?
[03:59] Sana: Mixtral has shown strong multilingual capability and good throughput; smaller footprint than 70B models but often better instruction-following than some older 13B models. It tends to quantize well, so latency drops on INT8/4-bit profiles.
[04:12] Marcus: For throughput, how much difference should we expect between a quantized 13B and a 35B on p95? Ballpark numbers are helpful for capacity planning.
[04:19] Sana: Ballpark	6ms on an A100-style GPU: 13B quantized (4-bit) p95 for a ~200-token response might be ~120-250ms depending on batching; 35B might be ~250-600ms depending on precision; 70B often crosses 800ms-1.5s unless you use optimized kernels and higher-end infra. Those are rough but we'll measure exact during bench.
[04:40] Priya: We also need exact token-costs and expected monthly spend for 100k queries / month.
[04:46] Ethan: We'll include per-token cost estimates in the benchmark spreadsheet, with adjustments for batching/caching. Important variables: average prompt tokens, response tokens, reuse of prefix cache for similar prompts, and model quantization. We'll provide scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go vs dedicated reserved capacity.
[05:04] Ana: On domain accuracy, if we see the smaller models drop below our EM threshold, would Redwood support a LoRA or adapter tune during the POC? That might be quicker than full fine-tune.
[05:14] Sana: Yes, LoRA/adapters are a common pattern. We can help run a quick LoRA on a subset if you provide labeled data. That will also be part of the quality sweep to quantify improvement.
[05:23] Marcus: Any pitfalls running in our VPC with KMS? We use AWS KMS + strict egress policies.
[05:30] Ethan: We have customers running exactly that. We'll need a service account and an IAM role; KMS calls add small latency (~tens of ms) on key fetches but not per-token. For Private deployments we can also support an HSM-backed KMS if required. We'll capture these in the run.
[05:45] Priya: Ok timeline: we need the bench numbers and recommended model for the pilot by Jan 10. Is that feasible?
[05:52] Ethan: Feasible. Proposed timeline: by Jan 4 we send the benchmark template and shortlist; Polaris provides sample data by Jan 5; January 6-8 we run hosted baseline runs; Jan 9-10 we run in-VPC/Dedicated tests and deliver results and cost model by Jan 10.
[06:08] Ana: That works. A couple more specifics: multilingual eval sets	6ms we can provide translations of ~200 QA pairs per language. Is that enough?
[06:16] Sana: That's a good starting point for relative ranking. Ideally include a mix of short factoid QA and longer synthesis prompts. Also include a small set of adversarial prompts to probe hallucinations.
[06:27] Priya: For evaluation metrics, let's capture EM/F1 for QA, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization tasks, and token-level latency/cost.
[06:36] Sana: Agreed. We'll add automated scoring and produce a dashboard with per-model breakdowns.
[06:42] Javier: One legal ask: ensure logs are redactable and that we can disable retention if needed.
[06:48] Ethan: Affirmative. For Dedicated/Private we support configurable retention and redaction. We'll include options in the security pack.
[06:55] Priya: Anything else on model selection? Are there licensing issues with Mixtral / Llama-3?
[07:00] Ethan: We'll include licensing notes. Some open models have restrictions, and for Llama-3 you'll want to confirm their model license for commercial POCs	6ms Redwood tracks model license metadata and will surface any restrictions in the spreadsheet.
[07:10] Ana: Good. Can you also provide an expected cost delta between hosted eval vs Dedicated trial?
[07:15] Ethan: We'll calculate a back-of-envelope in the spreadsheet: hosted pay-as-you-go tends to be higher per-token but zero commit; Dedicated amortizes infra for sustained loads and will be cheaper at scale. We'll show scenarios for 100k and 1M queries/month.
[07:28] Marcus: From our side we'll prepare a small VPC with a test subnet and provide an IAM role for Redwood to run the Dedicated trial.
[07:35] Sana: Thanks	6ms we'll also include a minimal perf harness (Docker image + run script) so you can run locally if needed.
[07:42] Priya: Great. Let's reconfirm next steps.
[07:44] Ethan: Recap of next steps: Ethan will send the benchmark template and the initial shortlist (Mixtral, Llama-3 35B, Llama-2 13B quantized, Falcon 40B-instruct as optional). Sana will send the perf harness and instructions for multilingual labeling and scoring. Polaris provides dataset samples and network/KMS details. We'll schedule the hosted baseline Jan 6-8 and in-VPC Jan 9-10. Final results delivered Jan 10.
[08:08] Ana: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:10] Javier: Thank you.
[08:12] Ethan: Thanks all	6ms we'll follow up by email with the deck and documents.

End of call.
